body.claim: Göbekli Tepe, in Şanlıurfa Province, Turkey, was built around 9500 BCE, in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic. Its large circular structures contain large stone pillars.
body.why: The site was first used at the dawn of the southwest Asian Neolithic period. German archaeologist Klaus Schmidt recognised its significance in 1994 and began excavations the following year. Before that, attempts had been made to break up some of the pillars, presumably by farmers who mistook them for ordinary large rocks.
